newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbeks set to double gold output in 5-6 years.
newsitem.headline: Uzbeks set to double gold output in 5-6 years.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Uzbekistan plans to double its current gold production of around 60 tonnes a year over the next five to six years, a senior Uzbek gold official said on Tuesday.
"Uzbekistan may double output of gold in five or six years' time," Alexander Ogarkov of the State Geology and Mineral Resources Committee said in the capital Tashkent.

He said Uzbekistan was looking for foreign investment of around $1.1 billion to increase production and that extra output would come from planned and established joint ventures with foreign mining companies.
U.S.-based Newmont Mining Corp's Zarafshan Newmont gold project is already producing about one tonne of gold per month.
The Uzbek government is also finalising projects with Australia's Western Mining Corporation and Britain's Lonrho Plc, which Ogarkov said would produce similar amounts of gold.
Trade journals say the Central Asian nation is the world's ninth largest gold producer. Ogarkov said Uzbekistan ranked fourth behind Russia in terms of reserves.
